prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1099; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, if that's okay. You can just call me the claimant.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was stopped at a traffic light on a main road in Sugar Land, Texas, heading toward the shopping center.

Q: What happened next?

A: I was stopped with my foot on the brake, and then there was a hard impact from behind. My head snapped back and then forward. The other car's front end was pretty damaged.

Q: Did you exit your vehicle at the scene?

A: Yes, but I felt dizzy and sore, so I sat down on the curb until the police arrived.

Q: Did you receive medical attention that day?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that evening. They checked my neck and gave me a muscle relaxer and told me I had whiplash.

Q: Have you experienced any symptoms since then?

A: Yes. My neck is stiff, especially in the mornings, and I get headaches that start at the base of my skull. Turning my head to check my blind spot when I drive is hard now.

Q: Have you missed any work because of your injuries?

A: I missed about three days and I've been working reduced hours since. My job involves a lot of lifting, so that's been difficult.

Q: Are you currently seeing a physician or physical therapist?

A: Yes, I started physical therapy twice a week, and my doctor is monitoring my progress.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm trying to get back to normal, and I'd appreciate it if this claim could be handled promptly.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
